summary: Branch SFO edge NAT session pruning causing intermittent IPsec tunnel drops for on-prem services
description:
Issue summary:
Branch office (SFO) intermittent loss of access to internal on-prem services. Users reported that connections to internal dashboards and dev hosts drop after ~2-5 minutes; reconnecting restores service for a short window before the tunnel fails again.

Impact:
- ~12% of users on branch-sfo-01 experienced connection drops over morning hours (08:20-10:10 PT).
- Automated jobs that depend on the on-prem service failed and retried, causing transient load.
- No customer-facing production services impacted (internal-only).

Environment:
- Branch: branch-sfo-01 (Meraki MX > Palo Alto PA-5220 upstream edge).
- VPN: Site-to-site IPsec (IKEv2) from branch router to main DC vpn-gw-01 (us-west-2).
- Firmware: PA-5220 running PAN-OS 10.1.3 (edge), Meraki MX firmware 23.15.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) From branch workstation, initiate traffic to internal host behind vpn-gw-01 (10.10.40.0/24).
2) Traffic flows normally for ~2-5 minutes.
3) TCP connections hang; ICMP fails.
4) Router logs show UDP session removal due to age and IPsec peer DPD timeouts.

Observed behavior:
- Edge firewall log entries: "session deleted (UDP) age 31s, src=10.20.x.x dst=34.x.x.x:500" and periodic "NAT-translation pruned: session timeout exceeded".
- IPsec debug on branch: "IKEv2 child SA rekey attempted" followed by "no response from peer" then tunnel re-establishes briefly, later drops again.
- DPD (dead peer detection) probes often fail to traverse when NAT sessions are aggressively pruned.

Expected behavior:
- Persistent NAT mappings for IKE/ESP plus DPD keepalives should remain active for IKEv2 rekey/DPD intervals chosen by the tunnel.

Initial hypothesis:
- Upstream edge firewall configured with aggressive UDP session timeouts and a NAT cleanup policy that prunes related IKE/DPD mappings too quickly, causing the peer to appear unreachable during rekey/DPD.

Logs / evidence:
- Palo Alto system logs (excerpts provided in attachments): multiple "session idle-timeout" events at ~30s for UDP traffic.
- Router ipsec debug: repeated "Child SA not found" and "DPD initiator timed out" occurrences aligned with NAT prune times.
- Correlation with increased job failure rate in branch between 08:20-10:10 PT (Grafana alert graph linked).

Immediate mitigation performed:
- NetOps temporarily increased UDP session timeout on the PA-5220 from default 30s to 3600s for NAT policy matching IKE/UDP-ENCAP.
- Configured explicit NAT exemption for IKE/ESP traffic between branch-sfo-01 and vpn-gw-01 subnets.
- Reduced branch DPD interval to 15s and increased retransmit counts (to ensure quicker detection and fewer false positives).

Permanent fix applied:
- Rolled firewall template update to all Palo Alto edges in the SFO cluster to: 1) set UDP session timeout for IKE-related flows to 3600s, 2) add NAT-exempt rules for site-to-site IPsec endpoints, 3) increase per-policy tcp/udp session thresholds to avoid early pruning for known long-lived tunnels.

Follow-up actions:
- Create a runbook entry in Confluence for "Branch VPN: NAT timeouts and IPsec keepalive tuning" (linked).
- NetOps to validate other branch edges for the same PAN-OS default and schedule template push.
- Add an automated check in infra-monitoring to alert when IKE rekey count or DPD events exceed a threshold in a sliding window.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 08:40: Initial page from branch support; intermittent drops.
- 2026-03-10 09:05 Reproduced issue with packet captures (tcpdump on branch router) showing NAT translation entries expiring ~31s after last UDP packet.
- 2026-03-10 09:40 Applied temporary UDP timeout increase (NetOps) — immediate reduction in reports.
- 2026-03-11 10:00 Ran controlled test for 4 hours; no drops after NAT exemption policy applied.

Technical details:
- Root cause: PAN-OS default session aging + a matching NAT rule caused the firewall to prune UDP mappings used by IKE/DPD during rekey windows. IKEv2 rekey/DPD expects transient UDP mappings to stay alive long enough for the exchange; pruning caused half-open states and repeated re-establishment attempts.
- Alternate factors ruled out: no upstream packet loss, Meraki MX health metrics OK, no client Wi-Fi disassociation pattern matching timeframe.

Resources consulted:
- Palo Alto KB on session timeouts and IPsec: internal link.
- Captures uploaded to /shared/network/captures/INT-918476/

resolution: Root cause was aggressive UDP/NAT session pruning on the Palo Alto edge which removed IKE/DPD mappings during rekey windows. Resolved by adding NAT-exempt rules for IPsec endpoints, increasing UDP session timeout to 3600s for IKE flows, and rolling a firewall template to the SFO edge cluster. Runbook and monitoring tasks created for follow-up.
resolution_notes: Applied config changes during maintenance window. No further incidents in 72h window. NetOps to deploy template to remaining branch edges and validate. Created Confluence runbook and a GitHub PR to add an infra-monitoring check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-monitoring/pull/142
